title: Senior's toolkit: finding your way
summary: The discovery commands that answer "which command, which parameter, what does it return?" in seconds.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: finding your way
steps.body: Experienced people rarely remember syntax; they know how to ask the shell. These are the questions and the commands that answer them.

toolkit.what: Which command does X? Searches cmdlets, functions, aliases and programs on the PATH.
flags: search by half of the name
every command with this name, and which one wins

toolkit.what: How do I use it? Examples, one parameter, or the full page.
flags: type, position, pipeline input, wildcards allowed
the current page in a browser

toolkit.what: Downloads the full help (only summaries ship with PowerShell).
flags: no admin needed (the default in PowerShell 7)
English help on a localised machine
download once, then `Update-Help -SourcePath` on offline servers

toolkit.what: What does it return? The type and members of whatever comes down the pipe.
flags: static members of a type: `[datetime] | Get-Member -Static`

toolkit.what: What does this shortcut stand for (and which aliases does a command have)?
Is this verb approved for my function name, and what group is it in?
flags: Start, Stop, Restart, Enable, Disable, Install, ...

toolkit.what: A form for a command's parameters, which then writes the command line for you. Windows only (it is a WPF window).
flags: fill in a form, press Copy or Run

toolkit.what: The linter: aliases, unapproved verbs, plain-text passwords, unused variables, and many more.
flags: rewrite what it can (aliases, some formatting)
exit code = number of findings, for CI

pairs: Which commands can read a file's last lines?
What properties does this object have?

steps.prompt: Find every command in the Archive module, then read one parameter's help.
steps.explain: `-Module` lists what a module exports; `-Parameter` prints one parameter's details: its type, whether it is required, and which values it takes.

steps.prompt: `Get-Help Some-Command -Examples` shows only a syntax summary and no examples. You are offline on a server. What is the right fix?
options: On a machine with internet, `Save-Help -DestinationPath \\fileshare\help`, then on the server `Update-Help -SourcePath \\fileshare\help`
Copy the module's .psm1 file to the server
steps.explain: Help files are separate downloads. `Save-Help` and `Update-Help -SourcePath` are made exactly for air-gapped servers.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before searching the web, ask the shell: `Get-Command *thing*`, then `Get-Help <command> -Examples`, then pipe a result to `Get-Member`. It is faster, it is the version you actually have installed, and it works on a server with no browser.
